report.question: Developer request: bring the compiled donor’s dash into JUJUMP while retaining its timing and the platformer’s own physics. Recover a NEW standalone motion candidate. Prefer a compact experiment program to inspect the binary and chosen function bodies and run a checkpoint-bound controlled memory comparison. Choose hypotheses, code and inputs yourself. In a later model turn, use the actual result to choose evidence or a follow-up. Select inspected code and execution evidence, submit source, inspect real development first divergences and revise if needed. Use cooldown and remaining as the timer state field names for the current recipient instrumentation; infer their values and rules. Freeze a development-passed candidate and call separate acceptance, then conclude with actual experiment citations. The host checks the recipient only after recovery; you cannot claim recipient success. No pre-existing recovered implementation is available. Report incomplete work honestly; mapped fields, ABI, evaluators and recipient adapter are human assistance.

messages.text: Recovering donor dash timing — inspecting code and running paired motion trials.
First trials ran inactive — digging into traces and binary structure.
Recovering your dash motion — inspecting donor code and measuring real movement to nail timing.
Initial code scan done — now digging into the core motion logic and dash traces.
Recovering donor dash timing — probing motion traces and code to build your standalone component.
Early traces show walk and dash displacements — now digging into the update logic and timer state.
Probing the donor's dash timing to pin down the full motion.
Dash reads 7.5 px/frame — now tracing its full duration and cooldown.
Decoding your dash timing — walking speed and burst confirmed, now pinning the tail frames.
Dash window mapped — 8 frames at high speed, cooldown held then ticking down. Now hunting the direction logic.
Decisive dash timing captured — selecting evidence to lock the rebuild.

Conclusion from recorded evidence only. No standalone candidate was submitted, no development pass, no freeze, no acceptance ran. No recipient claim is made.

Actual evidence cited:
- Inspected code: binary:func11 ($update), binary:func21 ($f21) under selection-1.
- Controlled trial: experiment-b152959f-bfc4-4510-955e-71aa7422aaca (artifact 8e3bb01f899590dc49b3b38a1a8175976696f0ae8a4455096e46e5950c9bc852, checkpoint cp-e455535d13c256492d44 boot). Reproducibility-control pair; control==intervention as expected.
  - Start: X held frames 36-45: position 0,0, direction 0,0, cooldown 10->1, remaining 0.
  - Walk right (32) frames 46-48: +2/frame x (0->2->4->6), cooldown 0.
  - Frame 65 still walking: x=40.
  - Dash press (33=X+right) frame 66: x=47.5 direction 1,0 cooldown 25 remaining 7; then 55/62.5/70/77.5/85/92.5 (+7.5/frame) remaining 6..1, frame 73 x=100 remaining 0 cooldown 25, frames 74-76 +2/frame walk while cooldown 24->22. Final frame 85 x=124 cooldown 13.
  - selection-1 summary rule: walk 2/frame, dash 7.5/frame x8 frames remaining 7..0, cooldown 25 then 1/frame decay, X edge starts dash.
- Reproducibility controls: experiment-509c58bf-a684-4bc7-bb47-94a0477a2e02, experiment-4bf81f62-b59c-4f91-8e6d-2584ca64e067 showed 0 active updates / no events for their inputs; inactive endpoint not proof of no activity. Their full traces remain in artifacts fe1afe68..., 5a7e6b26... but were not read frame-by-frame here.

Remaining uncertainties / incomplete:
- Vertical (up 64 / down 128), left (16), diagonal dash vectors, dash distance/cooldown defaults, initialCooldown, float32 accumulation, exact dash-start/dash-end event names/timing, ownsMotion semantics, behaviour when X pressed without direction, during cooldown, or held vs edge, and walking while remaining>0 not established from reads above.
- Code bodies for func11/func21 were enumerated/inspected but full instruction semantics not decoded here; func13/func158 also inspected but not selected.
- Next required steps unexecuted: select evidence already done (selection-1) but submit_component_candidate, development revisions, freeze, acceptance all missing. No budget remains in this run.

args.hypothesis: Orientation plus controlled motion observation for dash and walk
args.source: const ov = await sdk.static.inspectWasm({view:"overview",startLine:1,lineCount:10}); const lf = await sdk.static.listFunctions({startIndex:0,limit:50}); let fi = 0; for (const f of (lf.functions||[])) { const n=(f.name||"").toLowerCase(); if (n.includes("update")||n.includes("step")||n.includes("tick")||n.includes("player")) { fi=f.index; break; } } if (!fi && lf.functions && lf.functions.length) fi = lf.functions[0].index; const code = await sdk.static.inspectFunction({functionIndex:fi,startLine:1,lineCount:100}); const de = await sdk.static.decompileFunction({functionIndex:fi,startLine:1,lineCount:100}); const cg = await sdk.static.callGraph({functionIndex:fi,direction:"callees",depth:2}); const prep = await sdk.prepareCheckpoint({hypothesis:"baseline checkpoint for dash walk",steps:[{buttons:0,frames:30,checkpoint:"cpbase"}],watches:[]}); const exp = await sdk.runExperiment({hypothesis:"walk right then dash press X motion timers events",checkpointId:prep.checkpointId,interventions:[],steps:[{buttons:32,frames:20,checkpoint:"walk"},{buttons:33,frames:10,checkpoint:"dash"},{buttons:0,frames:20,checkpoint:"rest"}],observations:{channels:["motion","timers","events"],watches:[],captures:[]}}); const exp2 = await sdk.runExperiment({hypothesis:"walk left up down coverage",checkpointId:prep.checkpointId,interventions:[],steps:[{buttons:16,frames:15,checkpoint:"left"},{buttons:64,frames:15,checkpoint:"up"},{buttons:128,frames:15,checkpoint:"down"}],observations:{channels:["motion","timers","events"],watches:[],captures:[]}}); return JSON.stringify({ovExports:(ov.exports||[]).length,funcCount:(lf.functions||[]).length,chosen:fi,codeExcerpt:JSON.stringify(code).slice(0,1200),deExcerpt:JSON.stringify(de).slice(0,1200),graph:JSON.stringify(cg).slice(0,800),cp:prep.checkpointId,exp:exp,exp2:exp2});
